column1: # Measured seconds per cargo test target, read by `tools/ci/test-shards.sh` to
# balance the CI shards by COST instead of by count
# (#2075). Four tab-separated columns, keyed exactly like the script's own
# inventory row so the join cannot be ambiguous:
#   <package>
# The metric is what a shard actually pays: the wall clock of ONE
# `cargo test <line>` invocation for that target — its build AND its run. That
# is usually larger than the 900s in-process guard, which bounds only the
# running test binary; a weight over 900 is not a licence to raise that guard.
# Rules:
# - MEASURED seconds only. A guessed number is a shard split that lies about its
#   own cost, and nobody ever revisits a guess. A target with no row here is
#   charged DEFAULT_WEIGHT (30s) — scheduled, never skipped — so an unmeasured
#   monster shows up as a visibly skewed real CI run and gets measured.
# - Measure on the builder host, one target at a time, and round UP:
#     scripts/agent/time-suites.sh <target>     # e.g. golden; guard stays 900s
# - Re-measure after anything that changes a target's cost. #2074
#   (content-addressed Prelude/Core rlibs) will cut the AOT-heavy targets by
#   most of their wall clock; every row below is stale the day it lands.
# - Rows are sorted by package, then kind, then target.
# Provenance of the seeded row:
# - `jet test golden`: docs/research/test-suite-performance-2026-08-08.md
#   measures the target at 45-90 min on a full supported host (479 example
#   entries, ~476 native AOT compilations). Recorded at the 45-min low end
#   (2700s) — the conservative end, because overstating one target starves the
#   other shards. This target is why weighted splitting exists: it is atomic, so
#   until #2074 shortens it no assignment can bring the spread under 2x.
jet
